added_failures_note: Derived with reckon.crew.review.added_failures_from_gate_logs over the reviewed run's own gate logs named in its manifest baseline_suite and after_suite: arms/base.log reports FAILED case1, case2 and case5, arms/head.log reports FAILED case5 only, both are pytest format and both arms were reduced against their own # cwd: header, so the added set is empty and the count 0.

findings.text: non-blocking: the check's own call site was rewritten in a module the node was not fenced to (prompt.txt:85-90 declares promotion_checks.py, promotion_evidence.py, recovery_review_delivery.py and the test file only); reckon/crew/promotion_scope.py:454 lands a companion source file without acceptance so the promotion is not held, but the declaration the dispatch gave said "nothing outside them".

non-blocking: the pytest-program predicate inside the out-of-scope case5 guard was narrowed from `\bpytest\b` to a word-basename match, which was needed only because the test writes its record under a `pytest-of-<user>` temp home — arms/base.log quotes that cited record path — so the section's "leave that guard unrelaxed" is bent; case5 still refuses, so only the strict direction is verified.

non-blocking: the dry-run invocation report runs the same fill, so `crew complete --dry-run` on a review run writes review-gate.log into the run directory although no row will cite it, which is why the claim at promotion_records.py:308 that the log is captured "only where the promotion will cite it" does not hold on that path.

item_verdicts.diff: Read c1a5111bc06 and 3e144f8875 against base 39c52edbf7 commit by commit: c1a5111bc06 changes reckon/crew/promotion_evidence.py (+101/-4: `_command_runs_pytest` replacing `_PYTEST_COMMAND`, and `_derived_review_gate_log`) and reckon/crew/promotion_records.py (+53/-14: `run_id` on the evidence, the check now capturing its log, and `capture_log` on the fill), and 3e144f88 adds only the nine-line evidence fragment docs/evidence/fragments/the-crew-does-its-own-bookkeeping/review-promotion-derives-gate-s1.html.
item_verdicts.done_when: The measure is the four-case head arm with case5 still red on the unrelaxed guard; arms/base.log at 39c52edbf709fb345de519ffbdd6d477aa2a88ef reports 3 FAILED (case1, case2, case5) with "3 failed, 62 passed" and EXIT=1, arms/head.log at c1a5111bc06f912a7d1a56574379b7d43151104b reports exactly one FAILED (case5, on the same "reaches no pytest summary" guard) with "1 failed, 64 passed" and EXIT=1, so cases 1-4 pass at the head, case5 still fails on that guard, and the done_when's four named cases are exactly what the gate asserts.
item_verdicts.goal: The goal is to deliver section s1 as its done_when states — a review run's promotion derives the gate it carries rather than citing the JSON record as its own log; reckon/crew/promotion_records.py:294 `_review_record_check` now delegates to `_derived_review_gate_log` at reckon/crew/promotion_evidence.py:1588, which evaluates `test -s` over the delivered record and writes `review-gate.log` ending in a terminal `EXIT=<n>` line, so the check is performed and captured instead of cited.
item_verdicts.manifest: Read manifest.md in full — status complete, commits c1a5111bc06 and 3e144f8875, changed_paths naming three files, a literal tests: command, both arm logs under test_logs, baseline_suite/after_suite with revision, command, exit_status, completed, failure_count and ids, and negative_control_log at negative-control.log; its quoted figures "1 failed, 64 passed" and "3 failed, 62 passed" are the summary lines of arms/head.log and arms/base.log.
item_verdicts.write_paths: Read the declared paths in prompt.txt:85-90 and the same list in dispatch-detail.json node.write_paths (reckon/crew/promotion_checks.py, promotion_evidence.py, recovery_review_delivery.py, tests/test_a_review_runs_promotion_derives_its_own_gate.py, the s1 evidence fragment and its figure directory); the diff changes reckon/crew/promotion_evidence.py and reckon/crew/promotion_records.py and adds the fragment, so promotion_records.py:294 is the one path outside the nodes declaration, disclosed in manifest.md rubric.scope_discipline.

justifications.durability: negative-control.log reinstates the defect by returning the check to citing the stored record as its own log (the base form at promotion_records.py:302-306) and case1 reddens there with "carries no terminal EXIT=<n> line", an id absent from arms/head.log, while case5 holds the pytest-summary guard's strict direction.
justifications.evidence: arms/head.log ends in EXIT=1 with "1 failed, 64 passed" and arms/base.log in EXIT=1 with "3 failed, 62 passed", each header naming its revision, tree, module and cwd, and manifest.md records both arms in baseline_suite and after_suite rather than claiming them.
justifications.fit: the additions are private, docstringed helpers beside their neighbours at reckon/crew/promotion_evidence.py:1225 and :1588, use the module's own lazy-import idiom at promotion_records.py:316, and introduce no name outside the existing `_PYTEST_*`/`_REVIEW_*` private conventions.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/promotion_evidence.py:1631-1654 evaluates the `test -s` check itself rather than reporting a fixed exit status 0 as promotion_records.py:302-306 did at base, and the log it writes carries the `# command:` header the readers at promotion_evidence.py:1788-1800 parse.
justifications.reuse: searched reckon/crew for a writer of the gate-log capture shape and an existing pytest-program test — promotion_gate.py:_write_replay_log owns the re-run form of the same header+EXIT write and dispatch_watch.py:69 owns the `pytest-of-<user>` knowledge, and while neither is the owner of "capture a review's own check" (no such owner exists), `_derived_review_gate_log` also does not reuse `_write_replay_log`'s write, so it duplicates that shape.
justifications.scope_discipline: every hunk is in reckon/crew/promotion_evidence.py or the fragment except reckon/crew/promotion_records.py:286-331 and :460-470, which the declared write paths at prompt.txt:85-90 do not name.
